label: 男湯・女湯それぞれの定書
summary: 男湯用・女湯用の2種類の掲示文例。どちらも「預かり物は一切お引き受けしません」「右の通りご承知のうえでご入湯ください」と結ぶ、客向けの断り書き。末尾から「湯屋譲り申す証文の事」（店の譲渡契約書のひな形）がはじまる。上段の役員当番表は第六十四期（天保13年3月〜）で終わり、「大行事半年持ち」と添えられる。

sections.modern:
一、失せ物があっても、衣類の弁償はご勘弁いただきますので、ご用心ください。一、預かり物は一切お引き受けしません。右の通りご承知のうえでご入湯ください。以上。月日　ただし男湯の分。
続いてもうひとつの「定」。一、お上のご法度はかたくお守りください。一、火の元は大切に、念を入れてください。一、男女入込湯（混浴）はご禁制です。一、風の強い日は早じまいいたします。一、お年寄りや病み上がりの方は、湯あたりなさらないようご用心ください。一、衣類や持ち物は、どんな品でもご自分でご用心ください。一、失せ物・預かり物については一切責任を負いません。右の通りご承知のうえでご入湯ください。以上。月日　ただし女湯の分。
sections.english:
Item: Should anything go missing, please excuse us from compensating for clothing; take care yourselves. Item: We accept no items for safekeeping whatsoever. Bathe with the understanding that the above applies. That is all. [Month, day.] Note: for the men’s bath.
Then a second “Rules” notice. Item: Strictly obey the laws of the authorities. Item: Take great care with fire. Item: Mixed bathing of men and women is prohibited. Item: On windy days we close early. Item: The elderly and those just recovering from illness should take care not to be overcome by the heat of the bath. Item: Please look after your own clothing and belongings, whatever they may be. Item: We take no responsibility at all for lost articles or items left with us. Bathe with the understanding that the above applies. That is all. [Month, day.] Note: for the women’s bath.
sections.note: 男湯用・女湯用の2種類の掲示文例がセットで載っています。以前の版は「落とし物・預かり物は番台で預かる」と読んでいましたが、実際は「預り物一切不仕（いっさい預からない）」「うせ物并あづかり物一切致し不申候」で、意味が逆でした。両方の結びも「相守るべし」ではなく「右之通り承知之上、御入湯下さるべく候」——客に向けた「ご承知のうえでお入りください」という免責の断り書きです。女湯版はお年寄り・病み上がりへの気づかいなど、条文が細やか。「預り物一切不仕候事」と、年寄りの条の頭の「御年寄」は、国会図書館本の原寸画像と東書文庫本（別の刷り）の両方で字形が一致したので確定しました。男湯版の冒頭の条（「衣類之儀ハ御免可被下候間」＝衣類の弁償はご勘弁を）と、年寄りの条の後半（「湯あたり致さぬ様」）は、字形の残る部分とルビ「ごめん」、湯屋の貼り紙の定型から推測で補った読みです（｛｝の箇所）。
sections.noteEn: The book gives a matched pair of sample notices, one for the men’s bath and one for the women’s. An earlier version read “lost articles and items left for safekeeping are held at the bantai,” but the text actually says the opposite: “we accept no items for safekeeping whatsoever” and “we take no responsibility at all for lost articles or items left with us.” Both notices close not with “obey the above” but with “bathe with the understanding that the above applies”—a disclaimer addressed to customers. The women’s version is more considerate, with an article for the elderly and those recovering from illness. “Not accepting anything for safekeeping” and the opening words of the article on the elderly were confirmed by matching the character shapes in a full-resolution image of the National Diet Library copy and in the Tosho Bunko copy (a different printing). The first article of the men’s version (“please excuse us from compensating for clothing”) and the second half of the article on the elderly (“not to be overcome by the heat”) are conjectural readings, filled in from the partly visible characters, the printed reading gomen, and the usual wording of bathhouse notices (the parts in braces).

sections.english:
Here begins a model contract for handing a bathhouse over to someone.
“Item: This person, ____ by name, whose origins we know well and who is trustworthy,
sections.note: ここからは文書テンプレート集。目次にあった「売渡証文」「敷金証文」「奉公人請状」のひな形が順に並びます。書き出しは「此誰と申者」で、生国の後は「能存慥成者故（よく存じ、たしかなる者ゆえ）」と推測しました。次丁の「文人ニ相立」へ自然につながり、奉公人請状の書き出しと同じ型です（｛｝の箇所は推測で補った読み）。
sections.noteEn: From here on the book is a collection of document templates. The model deed of sale, security-deposit deed, and servant’s letter of guarantee listed in the Contents follow one after another. The deed opens “This person, ____ by name”; after “place of birth” we conjecture “being well known to us and trustworthy,” which runs naturally into “we stand as bunnin” on the next spread—the same opening as a servant’s letter of guarantee (the parts in braces are conjectural).
